extra.message: User-controlled 'filter' and 'query' path parameters are concatenated directly into a raw SQL string and executed via db.sequelize.query. Attackers can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. /v1/search/id/2' UNION SELECT ...) to read or modify the database.

req.query.picture is interpolated into a filesystem path ('../../../uploads/' + filename) and passed to fs.readFile without sanitization, allowing path traversal (e.g. picture=../../.env) to read arbitrary files on the server.
req.params.brand is concatenated into a shell command passed to child_process.execSync without escaping, enabling OS command injection / RCE (e.g. brand="bud | whoami").
User-supplied JSON body is passed to node-serialize's serialize.unserialize(), which executes serialized functions, allowing arbitrary code execution (RCE) via crafted payloads.
req.query.message is rendered with nunjucks.renderString(), allowing Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) which can lead to arbitrary code execution via Nunjucks object chaining.
req.query.message is rendered with nunjucks.renderString() in the /register route, allowing Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) leading to arbitrary code execution.

User-controlled 'message' query parameter is reflected into the page and rendered with the nunjucks 'safe' filter ({{ message | safe }} in user.html line 139), enabling reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
req.query.url is passed directly to axios.get without validation, allowing Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) to probe internal services and endpoints.
req.query.url is passed to res.redirect without validation, allowing an open redirect that can be used for phishing.
XML from user upload is parsed with libxmljs.parseXml(xml, {noent: true}), enabling external entity expansion (XXE) and potential file disclosure.

GET /v1/user/:id returns a user record (including password hash) by id with no authentication or authorization, allowing Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) to enumerate and retrieve other users' data.
GET /v1/order returns all beers with their associated user objects (db.beer.findAll({include: 'users'})), exposing PII including user password hashes (Excessive Data Exposure).
POST /v1/user/ assigns the client-supplied 'role' (req.body.role) directly to the new user record, allowing an attacker to self-register with role 'admin' (Mass Assignment / privilege escalation).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: PUT /v1/user/:id passes the entire req.body to db.user.update() with no authentication or field allow-list, allowing any user to modify arbitrary fields (including role) of any account (Mass Assignment / BOLA).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: DELETE /v1/user/:id has no authentication or authorization check, allowing anyone to delete any user account (Broken Function Level Authentication).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: PUT /v1/admin/promote/:id promotes any user to 'admin' with no authentication or authorization check, allowing vertical privilege escalation (Broken Access Control).

Admin endpoints (POST /v1/admin/new-beer/, /v1/admin/upload-pic/, /v1/admin/new-beer-xml/) require no authentication or admin role check, allowing unauthenticated users to create beers and upload files.

JWT is signed and verified using the hardcoded secret 'SuperSecret' (also at lines 251 and 404). Since the secret is publicly known in the source, any attacker can forge a valid token with role 'admin', bypassing authentication.
POST /v1/user/ stores the user's password in plaintext (password:userPassword) instead of hashing it. The /v1/user/login endpoint also compares plaintext passwords.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: The OTP validation logic is flawed: the seed is user-supplied (req.query.seed), the generated token is leaked back in the error response (line 421), and the check allows userToken == req.session.otp. This permits bypassing 2FA to obtain a valid JWT.
Session cookies are configured with secure:false and httpOnly:false, and a hardcoded session secret ('SuperSecret' at line 57), exposing sessions to interception, client-side theft, and forgery.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie Without Secure Flag

extra.message: The session 'genid' function derives the session id from a predictable timestamp or the existing req.session.uid, enabling session fixation / predictable session identifiers.
verifyToken uses jwt.decode() (which performs no signature verification) instead of jwt.verify(), allowing attackers to forge tokens by simply base64-encoding arbitrary payloads.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: POST /v1/admin/upload-pic/ uses multer with no file type, size, or content restrictions, allowing unrestricted file upload to the server (and the files are stored under ./uploads/).

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: The JWT secret fallback uses the bitwise OR operator (|) instead of logical OR (||), causing jwtSecret to evaluate to 0 rather than the intended 'superSecretPassword', and it embeds a hardcoded secret string.
